ideas: What the film is about and when you first saw it
Scenes or characters that stay with you
Why it feels different each time you watch

phrases.meaning: a film that makes you happy
feel meaningful or familiar to someone

model: A film I'd happily watch again is Spirited Away, the Japanese animated film by Hayao Miyazaki. I first saw it when I was about thirteen, on a rainy weekend at my cousin's house, and I've probably watched it five or six times since. The plot revolves around a ten-year-old girl called Chihiro, who gets trapped in a strange world of spirits after her parents are turned into pigs. She has to work in a bathhouse to save them, and along the way she becomes much braver. The first thing people tend to notice is the stunning visuals, because every scene looks like a painting. But what really strikes a chord with me is the idea of growing up and finding courage when you're scared. It's arguably one of the best animated films ever made, and it seems to me that it's stood the test of time really well, even though it came out more than twenty years ago. It isn't exactly a tear-jerker, but some scenes, like the quiet train ride across the water, do make me quite emotional. Every time I watch it, I pick up on something new, like a small detail in the background or a line I hadn't understood before. I'd say that's why I never get tired of it. To some extent, it feels different depending on what's happening in my own life.
